Requirement: Provide title/instructions, playing, paused and result states. Start, resume, restart and quit through documented keyboard controls.
Expected acceptance evidence: Pause freezes gameplay time and movement; restarting restores initial score, lives, timer and objects.

Requirement: Move one player in four directions using documented keys. Keep the player inside the arena or walkable map.
Expected acceptance evidence: At each outer boundary, another outward move leaves the player in bounds; diagonal speed tricks are unnecessary.

Requirement: Use five collectibles worth 10 points each and three predictable patrol hazards. Collect each item at most once.
Expected acceptance evidence: Collecting the same item twice changes the score only once; collecting all five yields 50 points.

Requirement: Begin with three lives and a 90-second active-play timer. A hazard hit removes one life, returns the player to the safe start and gives 1000 ms hit protection.
Expected acceptance evidence: A hit at 1000 ms leaves two lives; a second collision at 1500 ms leaves two; at 2000 ms it may remove one more.

Requirement: Win by collecting all five items and reaching the exit. Lose at zero lives or zero remaining time. Resolve loss before win if both occur in the same update.
Expected acceptance evidence: With the final item and exit reached while the timer expires, show loss. No further score changes occur after a result.

Requirement: Display score, lives, remaining time, controls and win/loss feedback. Mark player, collectibles, hazards and exit with shape or text as well as colour.
Expected acceptance evidence: A peer identifies each object and reads the current values without an audio cue or colour-only distinction.

Requirement: Use student-written functions with parameters/returns for state changes, collision consequences, scoring and results. Process a one-dimensional list of collectibles; own classes, nested grids and advanced libraries are unnecessary.
Expected acceptance evidence: Explain one function contract and trace removal/collected status for first, last and only remaining collectible.

Requirement: Append the final integer score once per completed run to a local text history. Read valid prior scores and show count, total and first maximum position; show an empty-history message.
Expected acceptance evidence: For [20,0,50,50], count 4, total 120, first maximum index 2. Missing history starts empty. Skip malformed/out-of-range score lines with a warning; a failed write reports failure and gameplay remains usable.

Requirement: Offer two pre-defined difficulty choices; normal patrol interval is 1000 ms and challenge is 750 ms. All other rules, counts, scoring and time remain the same.
Expected acceptance evidence: Unsupported menu keys do not start a run. The selected difficulty survives pause but restart resets the current run.

Requirement: Usability: instructions visible before play, a clear pause indicator, readable HUD at the agreed 800 × 600 test window and consistent restart/quit controls.
Expected acceptance evidence: Run a short peer trial; the peer starts, pauses and restarts using only the instructions. Record difficulties and one response.

Requirement: Reliability: run a two-minute repeatable trial including pause, restart and result states without an unhandled exception. Use a fixed layout and deterministic patrols for tests.
Expected acceptance evidence: Record the actual build, test sequence, result and any correction/retest. A pause long enough to cross 90 wall-clock seconds must not consume active-play time.

Requirement: Responsiveness: process close/keyboard events every frame, cap rendering with Clock.tick(60), and avoid blocking sleeps in the game loop.
Expected acceptance evidence: On the named school reference PC with the required object counts, a pause input is visible within 250 ms in five observations. Record the method and results; investigate misses rather than infer performance from the FPS cap.

Requirement: Maintainability: meaningful names and constants, one clear responsibility per function/method, comments explaining decisions and a concise README.
Expected acceptance evidence: A peer finds the score, timer and hazard-interval constants and identifies the scoring function without tracing the whole program.

Requirement: Portability and resilience: run offline with Python 3 and school-approved Pygame, relative resource paths and primitive-shape fallbacks.
Expected acceptance evidence: Run from a different parent working directory; remove decorative assets and confirm the full game still works using shapes/text.

Requirement: Accessibility and assets: sound is optional, colour is never the only signal, and static images/audio/decoration may be made with AI or replaced by Pygame primitives without a marking penalty.
Expected acceptance evidence: Mute audio and use the shape/text version. Log each external or AI asset, tool/source, date and relevant permissions. Do not assume generated assets are automatically free of third-party rights.

Requirement: Authenticity and privacy: the assessed game logic, data design and explanations must evidence the student’s own learning. Keep dated versions, backup, and a source/assistance log; use synthetic labels only.
Expected acceptance evidence: Explain and make a small teacher-selected change to the same project. Asset-generation permission does not decide whether AI code assistance is permitted; the issued school conditions do.
